https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/english_edit.title: Alleged Nvidia spy Alice Huang courted investors with promise of coveted GPUs
https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/english_edit.p1: Alice Huang, whom US intelligence authorities suspect of having been a spy for a Chinese intelligence agency, reportedly attracted investors to a large-scale data center project with confident predictions that she could obtain advanced artificial intelligence semiconductors from Nvidia. On Monday, the Financial Times reported that Huang held an investment briefing for Chinese investors in early 2025 for a Southeast Asian data center project worth hundreds of millions of US dollars. During the meeting, Huang and her business partner Kang Wei told the investors that there would be “no problem securing” stable supplies of Nvidia’s advanced graphics processing units (GPUs). Kang Wei, Alice Huang’s business partner, currently sits on the board of the state-controlled Guilin Bank. Some have suggested that Alice Huang was able to promise access to Nvidia’s advanced chips, which companies around the world are scrambling to get their hands on, because of her extramarital relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Figures who attended the pitches said Alice Huang also played up her close ties with Alibaba, China’s largest e-commerce company, while courting investors. Alibaba had been a key client of Megaspeed, the company she ran, since Megaspeed first began offering cloud services in Southeast Asia. In 2024, Alibaba lent a hefty US$3 billion to Megaspeed’s Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix, through Apex Enterprise Solutions, its own Singaporean subsidiary. The loan fueled a dramatic expansion: Megaspeed’s assets, which stood at US$33 million at the start of 2024, had grown more than 90-fold by the end of the year. The Straits Times reported on Tuesday that when allegations first surfaced in October 2025 that Megaspeed had helped smuggle Nvidia chips into China, its office in an upscale building in Singapore’s central business district had already been emptied of staff. A profile of Alice Huang on Simuwang, a Chinese private fund database, says she worked as a reporter for outlets including Hunan TV, then moved to CITIC Securities and later handled investments at Shanghai Hexi Investment Management. None of that work history has been verified. The New York Post reported that it contacted Hunan TV and other outlets but could not confirm that Alice Huang had ever worked there.
